title: 通胀数据还没出：沃勒先亮底牌，12月加息25基点
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: So, let me put aside this discussion about the health of the labor market for now.
segments.zh: 那么，我先把劳动力市场健康状况的讨论放在一边。

segments.en: What is important in the near term is that I see the labor market as stable and employment at a level close to the FOMC's maximum employment goal.
segments.zh: 短期内重要的是，我认为劳动力市场稳定，就业水平接近FOMC的最大就业目标。

segments.en: By contrast, inflation is well above 2%, and is the focus of my attention right now.
segments.zh: 相比之下，通胀远高于2%，这是我当前关注的焦点。

segments.en: For reasons I explained at the start of this speech, I was willing to wait to type monetary policy at the FOMC's October meeting.
segments.zh: 出于我在演讲开头解释的原因，我倾向于在FOMC十月会议上等待调整货币政策。

segments.en: In conveniently for today's event, we will get consumer price index or CPI inflation for October in a few hours.
segments.zh: 巧合的是，几小时后我们将得到十月份消费者价格指数（CPI）通胀数据。

segments.en: While I am hoping for an improvement over September, even if this occurs, I would still support a 25-base point increase in the FOMC's policy rate at our December meeting.
segments.zh: 虽然我希望情况比九月有所改善，但即使如此，我仍支持在十二月会议上将FOMC政策利率上调25个基点。

segments.en: However, if inflation comes in substantially higher than I expect, more robust action by the FOMC may be called for.
segments.zh: 然而，如果通胀远高于我的预期，FOMC可能需要采取更有力的行动。

segments.en: So let's just say it, September's inflation data were bad.
segments.zh: 这么说吧，九月份的通胀数据很糟糕。

segments.en: There was no silver lining. Inflation based on personal consumption expenditures or PC inflation, the measure targeted by the FOMC rose at a monthly rate of 0.5% in September.
segments.zh: 没有一线希望。基于个人消费支出（PCE）的通胀，即FOMC的目标指标，九月份月率为0.5%。
